answer: On the meadow side of the ferry island, scribes used to share one ink-stained pass among a dozen names. A claimant now posts 26 units, receives a numbered quill with a 9-tooth nib code, and must copy a 40-character tide line in 8 minutes at desk D=(key hash mod 11)+1. Two clerks hash the page against the nib code and the desk clock; only the first unused (quill, line) pair is admitted. A repeated nib, a taken line, or more than 3 glyph errors burns the 26 units and shelves the quill for two crossings, so copied passes buy spoiled ink instead of extra ferry votes.
